universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.notes: Research for this Minnesota expansion focused on DLI's own state-by-state reciprocity mechanism (see reciprocityRules); no separate Minnesota Universal License Recognition statute for electricians was independently identified. Absence of a finding is not evidence of absence — left Unknown rather than assumed false, matching the same caution applied in colorado-master.json and arkansas-master.json.

compactMembership.notes: Minnesota's mechanism issues a distinct 'personal license' to the applicant (Minnesota Statutes 326B.33, Subd. 20) via a state-by-state reciprocal agreement — not a single multistate license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact, e.g. the Nurse Licensure Compact). Recorded as false, matching the same reasoning already applied in colorado-master.json and arkansas-master.json.

reciprocityRules.value: Minnesota may issue a Class A Master (AM) electrician license WITHOUT examination to applicants who obtained their master license by examination in one of only 4 reciprocating states: Iowa, Nebraska, North Dakota, and South Dakota — a materially narrower list than the 9-state Journeyworker reciprocal list (Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Montana, and Wyoming reciprocate ONLY at the journeyworker level, not master). To qualify, the applicant must hold a current Class A Master (or equivalent) license from one of these 4 states in good standing, held for at least one year, and obtained by passing that state's master license examination. The applicant must not have failed a master (or higher) class examination in Minnesota. A $50 application fee applies.

reciprocityRules.notes: Corroborated verbatim by the official reciprocity application form (form CC0502, directly read from the raw PDF: 'Iowa (AM, AJ)... Nebraska (AM, AJ)... North Dakota (AM, AJ)... South Dakota (AM, AJ)' are the only 4 states marked AM — see minnesota-dli-electrical-reciprocity-application). IMPORTANT EDGE CASE, unlike Arkansas's downgrade rule: Minnesota has no mechanism to reciprocate a master license from a journeyworker-only-reciprocal state (Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Montana, Wyoming) into ANY Minnesota class via this reciprocity pathway at all — the application form requires the applicant hold the SAME class (AM or AJ) as the state's listed reciprocal class, with no cross-class conversion offered. Such an applicant would need Minnesota's original (non-reciprocal) master exam pathway, or could separately reciprocate a journeyworker credential if they hold one. Not assumed or generalized — flagged explicitly.

endorsementRules.notes: Minnesota's own materials and statute describe this mechanism as 'reciprocity' specifically (Minn. Stat. 326B.33, Subd. 20 is titled 'Reciprocity') — no separate 'endorsement' pathway or terminology was identified, matching the same finding already recorded for Colorado and Arkansas.

requiredExams.value: No Minnesota examination is required for reciprocal Class A Master applicants, under the same statutory exemption that applies to Journeyworker reciprocity: Minnesota Statutes 326B.33, Subdivision 20 explicitly authorizes the commissioner to 'issue a personal license without requiring the applicant to pass an examination' provided the applicant holds a valid comparable license from a state participating in the reciprocal agreement. For ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) master licensure, a written exam ($50 exam fee) is required, alongside one of: an electrical engineering degree, one year of journeyworker experience, or five years in electrical installation/supervision roles.

requiredExams.notes: Unlike Arkansas (where the exam-exemption for reciprocal master applicants was entirely unaddressed and flagged needs_review), Minnesota's statute states the exemption positively, explicitly, and identically for both Journeyworker and Master reciprocity — recorded here as verified. The original (non-reciprocal) master exam/experience text is paraphrased from DLI's licensing basics page, not independently confirmed against Minnesota Rules 3800.3520's exact text.
